channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Spain begins three days of mourning after train crash kills 69
item.description: Spain's second high-speed rail disaster this year, in which one train struck another from behind, killing 69 people, has raised fresh concerns about the safety of the country's rail network ahead of a national election. Three days of mourning have begun in the country.

item.title: Israelis await final election results as difficult choices lie ahead
item.description: Israelis awaited the final election results on Thursday to confirm what appeared to be taking shape: neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies nor the array of parties seeking to oust him seemed likely to secure a majority of seats in parliament. FRANCE 24's Clovis Casali reports from Jerusalem.

item.title: Spain's train crash kills 69 people: What exactly happened?
item.description: In Spain, the deadly train accident that killed 69 people and injured scores has once again brought national railway safety under the spotlight. Spain’s transport minister reported an "error" and "inexplicable circumstances" that led to one of Europe's deadliest train disasters this century.

item.title: US 2026: Georgia’s African Americans mobilise for the midterms
item.description: This is one of the key states in the US midterms. In Georgia, Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff’s seat is on the line – and with it, perhaps, the Senate majority. African Americans, who make up around a third of Georgia’s electorate, are being urged to vote early.

item.title: US economy grew at 3.4% annualized rate in 3rd quarter, government data shows
item.description: The United States economy expanded at an annualized rate of 3.4% over the three months ending in September, according to a government report released on Thursday.

item.title: USA: Barack Obama slams Donald Trump in final midterm push
item.description: Just five days before the US midterm elections, former president Barack Obama came to Georgia in a show of support to Senator Jon Ossoff in tthe midterm elections. Obama commented on the reaction of Trump's administration to a joke he had made the day before. "He was very upset about the Cheesecake Factory comments", Obama said. "They mobilized a whole-of-government response to that joke. Not to inflation, but to that joke." As the election is getting closer, polls point to a possible Democratic majority in the House.

item.title: Police to examine Thomas Markle's digital devices after child sex abuse image claims
item.description: Police in the Philippines have been handed a warrant by a court to start examining digital material alleged to contain child sex abuse images belonging to the Duchess of Sussex's father, Thomas Markle Snr.

item.title: Midterm elections live updates: Trump heads to Ohio, Obama rallies in Georgia
item.description: Trump heads to Ohio to rally with candidates in competitive races in the state.

item.title: Alaska governor orders probe into alleged effort to confuse Senate voters
item.description: Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy is ordering an investigation into an effort to recruit candidates for the Senate race, including one with the same name as the sitting senator.

item.title: 'Feels like being hit by a bus': Rib remodelling beauty surgery on the rise
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Thursday, October 29: Spanish papers discuss Wednesday's deadly train collision. The New York Times investigates whether a "safest seat" in the event of a train crash exists. Next, we look at a report about "the shocking rise of rib remodelling". We end with some photos from the Arctic and Antarctica.

item.title: WATCH: Obama slams Trump for getting mad at his Cheesecake Factory comment
item.description: The former president took issue with how President Donald Trump responded to his joke about "the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory."

item.title: Senate skeptical about making daylight saving time permanent despite Trump's pressure
item.description: Get ready to fall back

item.title: At least 13 killed in 'horrific' Russian drone strike at Ukraine train station
item.description: At least 13 people were killed when a Russian drone struck a busy railway station in Ukraine's Dnipro on Thursday, President Volodymyr Zelensky said, describing the attack as "horrific" and urging Kyiv's allies not to ease sanctions on Moscow.

item.title: Could she stand? Lagarde quits European Central Bank ahead of French election
item.description: The French head of the European Central Bank (ECB) is to step down from the role, just months ahead of the troubled country's presidential election.

item.title: Paris neighbourhoods: Exploring the lesser-known side of the 18th arrondissement
item.description: In this edition of French Connections, Genie Godula and Florence Villeminot continue their tour of Paris with a stop in the 18th arrondissement. The district is famous for landmarks like the Sacré-Cœur Basilica and the Moulin Rouge, but in this show we step away from the picture-postcard version of Montmartre and take you to see the rest of the 18th. We visit the vibrant multicultural neighbourhood called the Goutte d'Or, then take you to the largest fabric store in the world and introduce you to some of the 18th's most famous residents over the years. Join us as we explore the lesser-known side of the 18th arrondissement.

item.title: WATCH: Maine’s loggers and fishermen speak up about tariffs and higher diesel costs
item.description: ABC News’ Jay O’Brien talks to Maine Senate candidates Troy Jackson (D) and Sen. Susan Collins (R), as well as to fishermen and loggers impacted by tariffs placed on machinery imported from Canada.

item.title: WATCH: These dogs just love a pile of leaves
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a family from Maine that makes sure their yard always has a leaf pile ready for their two leaf-loving dogs.

item.title: Social media watchdog sets out age verification plans ahead of under-16s ban
item.description: Social media age checks could help protect under-16s from inappropriate online content, but some children may find ways round them, Ofcom has said.

item.title: REPLAY: French anti-terrorism prosecutor gives press conference on racist attack
item.description: The French anti-terrorism prosecutor, Olivier Christen, gave a press conference on Thursday about the recent racist terrorist attack that killed one man and wounded five others, including a 12-year-old girl, in Trappes. Watch our replay.

item.title: France reclaims title as Europe's champion of tax and social charges
item.description: New data shows that France has the EU's highest tax burden at 46 percent of GDP, while its national debt continues to grow. Amid new street protests over lack of education funding and falling purchasing power, the government is proposing a meagre hike in the minimum wage. Also in this edition: US tech giants see their shares diverge as the AI boom pushes massive capital expenditures.

item.title: Kenya's female athletes make their mark as Youth Olympic Games approach
item.description: Senegal is preparing to host the Youth Olympic Games, which begin this weekend. The young athletes who hope to showcase their talents on the international stage have their sights set on the Games, and Kenya has made sure that its young boxers remain on their toes and are ready to take on opponents of a higher calibre. FRANCE 24's Bastien Renouil reports from the ground.

item.title: 'There's clearly a marketplace for Russian in Africa - but it's not about institution building'
item.description: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Alex Vines, Africa Program Director at the European Council on Foreign Relations. He takes us through Russia's African paradox involving diplomatic Influence, security dependence and the politics of multipolarity. Moscow is gaining diplomatic traction across the continent even as its security partnerships, information operations and recruitment practices raise troubling questions about sovereignty, accountability and the human costs of geopolitical competition. For Vines, the participation of 48 African countries and 22 heads of state and government in the latest Russia-Africa summit illustrates the continuing appeal, of Moscow as a diplomatic and strategic partner.

item.title: Somalia: Lower house of parliament passes bill on sexual violence
item.description: The Somali Parliament has passed a new law against sexual violence. The country’s criminal code dated back to 1962 and had not been updated since. FRANCE 24's Bastien Renouil met with Sofia Rajab in Nairobi. She is the program manager at the NGO Legal Action Worldwide, an organisation that lobbied Somali authorities in support of this new law.

item.title: Spain train crash death toll rises to 69, emergency crews continue operations
item.description: Emergency responders continued operations on Thursday morning, following a deadly train crash in Spain a day earlier that killed at least 69 people. Victims of the deadly train crash were taken to the Institute of Legal Medicine of Toledo for identification. Police, medical and military units could be seen outside the institute, as FRANCE 24’s Sarah Morris reports.

item.title: Israel’s election committee urges probe into alleged Qatari interference
item.description: Israel’s Central Elections Committee has called on the Shin Bet chief to investigate allegations of foreign interference in the Knesset elections, including suspected funding and bribery linked to Qatar. FRANCE 24’s Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

item.title: WATCH: 'Liberty Biberty must go!' Protest over car insurance mascot
item.description: A small crowd took to the streets of Boston to protest against the existence of Liberty Biberty, the new fuzzy yellow mascot that appears in the insurance giant Liberty Mutual's TV ads.

item.title: From election defeat to Miami: What to know about Brazil's Bolsonaro's dramatic departure to the US
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro fled to Miami with his family after his defeat by Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Brazil’s presidential election. The 45-year-old ally of US President Donald Trump arrived in Florida on Wednesday, despite Brazil’s Supreme Court reportedly deeming him a flight risk amid ongoing corruption investigations and ordering his passports seized. FRANCE 24 International Affairs Editor Philip Turle explains what you need to know about the election and Bolsonaro’s departure.

item.title: Trappes residents reel from deadly racist attack that killed one
item.description: It's been five days since a gunman opened fire in a Paris suburb of Trappes in a suspected racist terror attack, injuring five and killing one. On the weekend, hundreds marched through the town in honour of the 26-year-old victim Pengo Bossio Wangi – and to show solidarity with his family. But the incident has left a deep mark on the local community, prompting the mobilisation of mediators to provide support.

item.title: Hong Kong leader apologises and housing minister resigns after fire investigation exposes failures
item.description: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee apologised on Thursday for a fire that ravaged a residential tower blocks in Tai Po in November 2025, killing 168, injuring 79 and displacing thousands of others. Housing Secretary Winnie Ho resigned Wednesday for her department's failure to supervise the maintenance work. A three-month investigation into conduct will follow, alongside proposals to criminalise bid rigging in relation to the complex's US $38 million renovation contract.

item.title: After years under fire, a rare quiet settles over Ukrainian city as truce holds
item.description: A planned six-day ceasefire brokered by US first lady Melania Trump and tied to a humanitarian aid mission in a Russian-occupied town has brought rare quiet to the Ukrainian-held city of Kherson across the water. A local pause in fighting started at 3am Tuesday to allow medicine, food and water to be taken to Oleshky before evacuation corridors are opened later in the week.

item.title: US cruise ship halts world voyage over fuel costs, 200 passengers stranded in Cambodia
item.description: Around 200 passengers who paid to live on a cruise ship while travelling the world were abruptly left in Cambodia after the company ran out of money. US-based operator Villa Vie Residences announced on Tuesday it was suspending operations of the Odyssey, two years after the ship set off, citing "extraordinary increases" in fuel costs following the US-Israel war with Iran.

item.title: ECB President Christine Lagarde to step down in February 2027, nine months before term ends
item.description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will step down on February 7, 2027, nearly nine months before her term expires, the ECB said Thursday. Her successor will be appointed by the European Council under EU treaty rules.

item.title: Suspect in Paris shooting to be placed in pre-trial detention, anti-terrorism prosecutor says
item.description: A shooter suspected of killing one person and wounding five others last week in the town of Trappes, near Paris, is set to be held in pre-trial detention and will appear before judges on Thursday, France’s anti-terrorism prosecutor said.

item.description: Artificial intelligence is making drones faster and more capable. Russia and Ukraine both use AI-powered drones, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned that AI could lead decisions on the battlefield as soon as next year. (Image credit: Paula Bronstein/for NPR)
